name: Field Doctor-Style Chicken Pad Thai (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
600 g Chicken
350 g Brown Rice Noodle [Brown rice flour, water]
340 g Beansprouts
2 1/4 Red Peppers
3 1/2 medium Carrots
210 g Edamame (SOY bean)
175 g Extra Virgin Olive Oil
95 g Ginger
55 g Brown Sugar
4 tbsp Lemongrass
3 1/2 tbsp Coriander
1 3/4 tsp Coconut Milk [Coconut, Water]
1/8 Lime Juice
2.7 g Chives
1/4 tsp Tamarind Extract
1/4 tsp Fish Sauce (Anchovy (FISH) (Encrasicholina spp), Salt, Sugar], Tamari [water, SOYA beans, sea salt], Lime Leaf, Red Chilli, Chicken Stock (Chicken Extract, Chicken Fat, Salt], Tapioca Starch, Fennel Ground, Coriander Ground, Sea Salt, Black Pepper
directions:
1. Noodles: Soak or boil brown rice noodles until just tender; drain and rinse so they don’t clump.

2. Sauce: Whisk tamarind extract, fish sauce, tamari, brown sugar, lime juice, coconut milk, grated ginger, lemongrass, lime leaf and a little chilli; loosen with water. Thicken lightly with tapioca slurry if you want it glossier.

3. Stir-fry: High heat, olive oil — cook chicken until done. Add carrot, red pepper and edamame; stir-fry tender-crisp. Add beansprouts and chives for the last minute.

4. Toss: Add noodles and sauce; toss quickly to coat. Finish with coriander.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Chicken Pad Thai (Low FODMAP) (~400 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/chicken-pad-thai
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~400 g x 8 = 3200 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~703 g (inferred ~21.96% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Extra Virgin Olive Oil is kept as an ingredient on this recipe because the ready meal is relatively oil-rich (or pesto-style); still fry/roast in extra virgin olive oil as directed.
